findings.finding: The methodological contribution says that the principal-minor hierarchy forces reciprocal-mean growth without stating the bounded-gradient and vanishing-predicted-decrease conditions required by the reciprocal-growth theorem.
findings.action: Qualify the sentence with bounded gradients and predicted decreases tending to zero. Prefer divergence of the mean, rather than generic growth. This changes the summary only, not a theorem or proof.
findings.disposition: recommended before the next satisfactory-exposition candidate

findings.finding: The explanation of the surviving smooth coordinate, comparison directions versus actual steps, accepted-run scope, the before/after mixed-benchmark comparison, and deterministic exclusions are each retold after the reader has already learned them. Section 6.7 and the beginning of Section 7 are particularly close in content.
findings.action: Keep the geometric explanation and initial lineage. Replace the global opening by a short transition to inward accuracy; reduce the post-benchmark paragraph to a precise one-sentence Guo–Lewis comparison. Consolidate deterministic exclusions in Section 7, retaining any unique strong-Wolfe/implementation restriction. Reduce the Section 7 positive summary to its two main answers and the nonradial extension. Preserve all theorem assumptions and proofs.
findings.disposition: recommended focused edit; estimated opportunity around 500–800 words, not a page-count promise

findings.finding: The cycle, covariance and all-query induction form a strong narrative, but the detailed scalar ramp formulas and their regularity proof interrupt that chain for roughly two pages. The parallel lower-curvature interpolation is already in an appendix.
findings.action: Optional structural improvement: keep the named scalar interpolation lemma and the scaling explanation in the main text, move its explicit definition and complete proof to an article appendix, and immediately define the objective and perform all-query induction. Move every defining formula and retain exact in-article references. This improves main-text continuity but does not reduce total length.
findings.disposition: optional; do not make this move merely to chase a page target

findings.finding: The introduction renders the named example as “example 9” although its environment is Theorem 9. The class also renders optional proof headings as “Proof (Proof of Theorem …)” and similarly for the appendix proof.
findings.action: Use “the example in Theorem” or “Theorem” for the introduction reference. Adjust the optional proof headings to the class convention, avoiding a repeated word Proof; a plain proof environment is sufficient when directly adjacent to its statement.

findings.finding: Some unpublished-source macros produce grammatical interruptions such as “examples in (authors, full title, manuscript)” and “see … in (full bibliographic mention)”. The load-bearing stable-manifold use has no theorem locator although an appropriate exact-version locator is available.
findings.action: Integrate author names into the sentence and put the full unpublished-work mention at a natural sentence boundary, preserving the current journal-policy treatment. Add Dyatlov 2018 v1, Section 3.5, Theorem 3, with the rescaling remark and Section 3.1 as appropriate to the local return map; do not cite the globally formulated Theorem 4 as if it directly had only the local hypotheses.
findings.disposition: recommended small scholarly repair; no evidence of a missing mathematical result
